## What is SoCal BOOM?

Southern California Biogeochemical Ocean Observations and Models—SoCal
BOOM—is an annual meeting for the regional marine-biogeochemistry community.
It welcomes work spanning global and regional questions, observations,
experiments, proxy records, theory, and numerical modeling.

## Mission

The one-day symposium brings together students, postdoctoral researchers,
researchers, and faculty from institutions across Southern California. Its
goals are to:

- highlight research led by graduate students and postdoctoral researchers;
- foster interaction between observational and modeling communities;
- support new regional collaborations; and
- provide an approachable setting for sharing work in progress.

Faculty and other senior researchers are encouraged to attend, participate in
discussion, and support early-career presenters.

## Research community

The meeting welcomes scientists across ocean biogeochemistry, including those
working in laboratories, in the field, with remote or proxy observations, and
with theoretical or numerical models. Participants are encouraged to explain
how their research connects measurements, mechanisms, and models of the Earth
system.

The fifth annual SoCal BOOM was held at UCLA on November 22, 2025.

*[Source: the 2025 SoCal BOOM homepage](https://socalboom.wordpress.com/).*
